name.text: Finding the mistake in a roof angle

questiontext.text:
The roof of a gazebo is a right pyramid VABCD on a square base of side {@ss@} m. Its height VO is {@hh@} m. Otieno wants the angle between the face VBC and the base. His working: [[if test="isE"]]OC = half of the diagonal AC = {@d2(OCr)@} m; \(\tan\theta = \frac{\mathrm{VO}}{\mathrm{OC}} = \frac{{@hh@}}{{@d2(OCr)@}}\)[[else]][[if test="isHf"]]OM = BC = {@ss@} m; \(\tan\theta = \frac{\mathrm{VO}}{\mathrm{OM}} = \frac{{@hh@}}{{@ss@}}\)[[else]]OM = \({@ss@} \div 2 = {@hs@}\) m; \(\tan\theta = \frac{\mathrm{OM}}{\mathrm{VO}} = \frac{{@hs@}}{{@hh@}}\)[[/if]][[/if]]; \(\theta = {@d1(shw)@}^\circ\).

(a) Which statement describes his mistake?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Find the angle between the face VBC and the base, correct to 1 decimal place. Keep full calculator accuracy until the final answer.

[[input:ans2]] \(^\circ\) [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
(a) {@STM(er)@}

(b) Face VBC meets the base along BC. VM and OM are at right angles to BC, so the angle is VMO. OM = \({@ss@} \div 2 = {@hs@}\) m and \(\tan \mathrm{VMO} = \frac{{@hh@}}{{@hs@}}\), so angle VMO = \({@d1(th)@}^\circ\).

questiondescription.text:
Three-Dimensional Geometry: finding the mistake in a roof angle

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.4: Identify the mistake in a worked calculation of the angle between a face of a square-based pyramid roof and its base, then give the right angle.

Core

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

feedbackvariables.text: nev: is(ans1 = "never"); cv: if ans1 = "edge" then vE else if ans1 = "half" then vH else vV;

truefeedback.text: VO is the right side to use: it is the height, at right angles to the base, so the sloping edge VC is not needed. The mistake is elsewhere. Check three things: the point of BC his triangle goes to, the length he used for the base of the triangle, and which angle of the triangle he found.

falsefeedback.text: That mistake would give \({@d1(cv)@}^\circ\), not his \({@d1(shw)@}^\circ\). Look again at the lines he used for the triangle.

feedbackvariables.text: okr: is(ans2 > 0 and ans2 < 90); rdn: float(ans2*%pi/180); omv: if okr then float(hh/tan(rdn)) else NA;

truefeedback.text:
[[if test="e1"]]

That is the angle you get by using OC, which goes to the corner C, instead of OM.

[[else]][[if test="hf1"]]

That is the angle you get by using the whole side for OM instead of half of it.

[[else]]

That is the angle between the face and the vertical line VO, not the base.

[[/if]][[/if]]

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="okr"]]

V is {@hh@} m above O. With your angle, the slope from V would reach the base {@d2(omv)@} m from O. The slope of the face VBC is measured to M, the midpoint of BC: how far is M from the centre O of a square of side {@ss@} m?

[[else]]

An angle between two lines, or between a line or plane and a plane, is between \(0^\circ\) and \(90^\circ\). Check your working and your calculator mode.

[[/if]]
